Do not contact another author or judge. Your final response is the user-facing review deliverable for preservation, not private scratch notes. Do not supply private reasoning or numerical scores.

Candidate Maple's initial001 failed readiness while initializing and produced no image; its final002 through008 all have images. There are15 candidate images plus the reference. Roof edit increases ridge rise above fixed eaves30%; bench slats widen25% with legs attached; trees move outward0.6 world X. Independent CPU checks of actual native vertices passed29/29 per candidate, confirming these edits, unchanged unrelated geometry and camera-view geometry consistency; do not present those as your own tests. All14 final captures passed native WebGPU with no WebGL attempts or GPU errors. Lighting and camera choices differ by author, so this compares authored outcomes and cannot isolate renderer quality/performance. Exact model identity and full authentic author-transcript export are unavailable; this is exploratory and cannot receive a formal score.
Use the common brief's qualitative criteria: reference shape/proportions/layout/framing; palette/material/lighting/shadow fidelity; coherent genuinely3D parts acrossviews; visible artifacts; and edit coherence. Review final candidates first, then note what the available initial evidence shows. Identify strengths and weaknesses with exact image paths/cases, distinguish observation from explanation, and do not attribute a defect to an engine without code/ablation evidence. You may state a narrow visual preference if supported, or a mixed result. Include confidence and caveats, and concise follow-up hypotheses with acceptance observations. Return a self-contained public-facing review around500-800 words, explicitly list which images you inspected, and confirm no files/processes/writes remain. Report useful results right away, before scratch notes. If work remains, use collaboration.send_message; otherwise return the result. Keep your status report short; complete the research and deliverable at the depth the task requires. If authorization is missing, or the reviewer denies an action for that reason, pause and report the exact action, target, and blocker to me. If I send <transcript_evidence> that authorizes that action and target, proceed; if already denied, retry the same tool call once. Don’t add the evidence to tool arguments. If the evidence is insufficient or the retry is denied, stop and report back. If you delegate that action, forward the block unchanged.
